adjudication_records.issue_text: UsernameForm no longer auto-skips for re-authenticating users without passkeys: gating on realm-wide passkeys flag instead of whether the user has a credential, causing extra username form for all non-passkey users in passkeys-enabled realms (UsernameForm.java:47)

That’s a concrete behavior/UX change grounded in the diff, but it’s not verifiably a correctness defect from the diff alone (it may be intentional to keep passkeys available during re-authentication).

While it is newly invoked from `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)`, the diff provides no evidence that these attributes “leak” beyond the current rendered response or “persist for subsequent forms” (they are not written back to session notes or any shared state in this helper). Whether `context.form()`/its attributes persist across subsequent challenges is not verifiable from this diff alone, so the claimed broken behavior cannot be confirmed here.

The finding’s claimed broken behavior (“identity-switch flows reusing the auth session… no way to change user”) is not evidenced anywhere in the diff: there’s no code showing such an identity-switch flow, no indication that this auth note would be set in that scenario, and no proof that hiding the username would eliminate all ways to change user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers the passkey-error + username-hidden combination from the new error-page behavior, leaving the rendered form contract change unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new UI-contract logic on error paths: `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse()` now calls `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` after enabling conditional UI, which (when `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` auth note is true) sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `REGISTRATION_DISABLED`. While multiple new tests cover re-authentication flows and password-error behavior, none exercise a *passkey failure* path (i.e., triggering `createErrorResponse`) and assert the resulting form renders with the username hidden/registration disabled in that scenario. So the new passkey-error + username-hidden combination is not verified by tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Conditional UI (passkey autofill) silently dropped on initial login page when user is not yet identified, since fillContextForm is only invoked when a user is already set — regression for username-less passkey login (UsernamePasswordForm.java ~113)

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, the diff changes when `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is invoked. Previously, the error-path `challenge(context, String, String)` explicitly called `fillContextForm` when `context.getUser() == null` (i.e., before user identification). Now both `authenticate()` and the error-path `challenge()` gate this on `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, whose implementation requires `user != null`. This means the initial username/password login page (no user set yet) will no longer have WebAuthn conditional UI context populated via this authenticator, matching the finding’s regression claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error challenge path loses WebAuthn setup when user lookup fails or user is null: new condition requires user != null, so failed login for unknown username no longer renders passkeys/conditional-UI markup (UsernamePasswordForm.java ~137)

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(context, error, field)` the condition to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` changed from `context.getUser() == null && ...passkeysEnabled` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. This means on error paths where no user is identified (e.g., unknown username / failed user lookup, leaving `context.getUser()` null), the WebAuthn/passkeys form setup will no longer run, so the passkeys/conditional-UI markup won’t be rendered on the error challenge page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NPE risk in UsernameForm.authenticate() which calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() unconditionally before the user-null check; if UsernameForm's webauthnAuth can be null (realms without WebAuthn), this could NPE on every login flow (UsernameForm.java:47)

adjudication.rationale: In UsernameForm.authenticate() the new condition is `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... }`. In Java, `&&` short-circuits left-to-right, so `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is only evaluated when `context.getUser() != null` is true. The finding’s claim that it is called unconditionally before the null check (and thus could NPE on every login) is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test no longer clears events between phases after logout(), so events.expectLogin().assertEvent() may match a login event from the first login phase instead of the re-authentication phase, allowing the test to pass spuriously (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java)

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java, the re-authentication assertions either (a) occur after a prior events.expectLogin().assertEvent() call (which typically consumes the login event, so it can’t be re-matched), or (b) are preceded by an explicit events.clear() before the relevant expectLogin() (e.g., in webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey(), events.clear() is called right before the passkey re-auth expectLogin, and again before the password re-auth expectLogin). There is no diff-shown case where logout() happens, events are not cleared, and then a later expectLogin() could spuriously match the earlier login event due to that missing clear.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey and reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey don't assert re-authentication mode rendering (USERNAME_HIDDEN / REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes) for the new AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError behavior, so a regression hiding setup errors would go unnoticed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/refactors re-authentication error-form setup into AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(), which conditionally sets LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED based on the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH auth note. This helper is now invoked from AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler() and WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(). The newly added/modified tests (including reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey and webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey) assert re-authentication via the info message and WebAuthn form presence, but they do not assert the specific rendering attributes that the new helper is responsible for, so a regression in that logic would not be caught. This is a concrete test-coverage gap tied to the new helper behavior, not a verified runtime defect in the implementation itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse (lines 49-54) calling setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError on failed passkey authentication during re-auth has no test coverage; failed passkey/WebAuthn re-auth scenario is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse` to call `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` on passkey failure, affecting how the username/password form is rendered during re-authentication. While several new tests cover *successful* passkey re-auth with `prompt=login` and password failures during re-auth (e.g., `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`, `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication`, and `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`), none of the added tests exercise a **failed WebAuthn/passkey attempt during re-authentication** that would trigger `createErrorResponse` and validate the re-auth form attributes are set. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2 Regression: conditional-UI setup lost when user is null in the error-challenge path — new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires user != null, so `fillContextForm` is no longer called for unknown/unset users, silently dropping passkey/conditional-UI form attributes (ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, autocomplete hints, webauthn form) after a failed login

adjudication.rationale: In `UsernamePasswordForm`, the PR changes both the normal challenge path and the error-challenge path to only call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` is true, and that helper explicitly requires `user != null` (`return ... && user != null;`). Previously, the error-challenge path *specifically* filled WebAuthn/passkeys context when `context.getUser() == null` and passkeys were enabled. With the new condition, unknown/unset users will no longer get `fillContextForm` invoked in the error path, so any passkey/conditional-UI form setup that depends on `fillContextForm` (e.g., attributes/UI wiring) will be dropped after a failed login when the user isn’t identified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding assumes `fillContextForm()` will execute the “empty authenticators” branch for conditional passkeys and thus add passkey-related errors/state for users without WebAuthn credentials. But this diff explicitly introduces `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context)` and overrides it in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` to always return `false` (“Do not show authenticators during login with conditional passkeys”). Also, in `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate()` the call to `fillContextForm` was already effectively gated by `context.getUser() != null` before; the main change is extending it to the error challenge when a user is present, which is aligned with the added re-authentication tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Double-check: the removed "passkeys disabled once user identified" protection (confirmed by the test change) may cause browsers to pop unusable passkey dialogs for non-passkey users due to empty-`allowCredentials` conditional-UI prompts

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the prior guard that only prepared/filled passkeys context when the user was *not* already identified: in `UsernamePasswordForm.challenge(...)` it changed from `if (context.getUser() == null && ...passkeysEnabled)` to `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))`, and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` explicitly requires `user != null`. Whether this leads to “unusable dialogs for non-passkey users due to empty allowCredentials” is not verifiable from the diff (no allowCredentials construction is shown), but the change does broaden when conditional-passkey UI is set up for identified users and may warrant checking behavior for users with no WebAuthn credentials, especially since `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` returns false and thus skips the existing empty-authenticator check in `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`.
